_doc: [ui2] Workbench tabs appear only once they are open (the owner: don't show what you can't use yet). A tab opens when ANY of its conditions holds, and stays open for good (flags.bench_tabs). Conditions: ["earned", N] lifetime cubes earned; ["stat", key, N] GameState.stats[key] >= N; ["hub_level", N]; ["flag", key]; ["always"]; ["builds"] something to build or built (HubBuilds, [ui3]). rockets is not a tab any more: it sets when the Upgrades tab shows its Rocket section. Other systems can add a gate in code: UpgradesScreen.set_tab_gate(id, func() -> bool, hint), which wins over this table. [v1guide] ["bench_tier", N] the workbench's tier; ["tower", N] the signal tower's tier. Owner 2026-11-08: tabs past Upgrades and Build open only by upgrading the workbench (tiers, ui/bench_tiers.gd): each tier lists the tabs it opens, its cost and what it waits for (requires: conditions, all must hold). grants_research: research the tier brings with it (the Bot Bay comes with Salvage Logic, so its first robot can be built before the Research tab opens). upgrade_order: the fixed order of the Upgrades tab's Lumi and machine rows (owner: rows never move by price); ids not listed follow in data/upgrades.json order. [M3-19] Tiers cost cubes only; the Bot Bay's 800 was the accepted proposal's price. [M3-21] Fitted to the game's real income (docs/reviews/M3-21_PACING_FIT.md): the Bot Bay costs 260 and waits for the tower and 6 clean hexes (the gate, not a dear price, keeps the first robot near minute 9 for the bot: a dear price is a long wait with nothing bought); the Research Desk costs 350 and waits for the seed tin as well as base level 2: fetching the tin takes Lumi off the work, and while the Desk was being saved for at the same time four runs bought nothing for 144 to 190 s. flag_hints: what a ["flag", key] requirement tells the player it waits for (ui/bench_tiers.gd requirement_text); a flag with no hint falls back to a general line.
